title: Tool signature translation and deprecation mapping for OpenAI-style tool calls
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers use a mix of OpenAI-style 'tools' (name + JSON Schema params) and older Redwood 'functions' endpoints. Differences include naming conventions (snake_case vs kebab-case vs spaces), implicit vs explicit parameter typing, streaming behavior during tool invocations, and how calls are identified in telemetry. This ticket implements runtime translation that preserves semantics, provides deterministic deprecation mappings, and adds a configurable fallback chain so existing customers don't break when switching models or SDKs.

Goals:
- Translate incoming OpenAI-style tool signatures to Redwood's legacy function surface (and vice versa for responses where needed).
- Provide a stable, customer-visible tool ID so rollouts/metrics don't flip when a name changes.
- Implement a deterministic collision resolution and aliasing policy (exact name, canonical alias, stable id, fuzzy match) with admin-configurable priority.
- Ensure streaming behavior for tool calls is consistent: start/partial/complete markers, KV-cache-safe streaming, and JSON chunk aggregation for structured outputs.
- Emit metrics and audit events for every translation/fallback so customers can identify misrouted calls and prompt regressions.
- Provide a migration helper (CLI + console view) to generate mappings for large customer tool sets and to preview the impact of deprecations.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts OpenAI-style tool list and routes calls to existing function handlers without code changes for customers that opt-in.
A stable 'tool_id' is emitted and persisted in traces/metrics for every tool call; changing tool name does not change tool_id.
Fallback chain honors configured priority and logs clear audit events when a fallback was used.

Streaming tool invocations send consistent markers (TOOL_CALL_BEGIN, TOOL_STREAM_CHUNK, TOOL_CALL_END) and downstream function handlers receive reassembled JSON or the original streaming chunks based on handler preference.
Migration helper produces a mapping file and a preview report that flags ambiguous name collisions and recommended aliases.

End-to-end tests cover: exact name route, alias route, stable id route, fuzzy-match route, streaming partial JSON reassembly, and malformed schema rejection with clear error code (400.compat-tool-schema).
Docs + SDK notes added to console docs and client SDK changelog with examples and recommended configs.
tasks: Design canonical tool_id format and storage (UUID + optional namespace).
Implement name-to-tool-id translation table with admin CRUD APIs in control plane.
Add runtime translation layer on request ingress to map OpenAI 'tools' -> function descriptors; preserve original payload on logs for audit.
Implement configurable fallback chain (exact_name, canonical_alias, tool_id, fuzzy_match) and corresponding metrics counters.
Streaming contract: define token-level markers and update runtime streaming path to attach marker metadata to events.
Build migration helper CLI that scans customer tool manifests and suggests mapping/aliases; include dry-run mode.
Create integration tests and a canary rollout plan for Dedicated customers with opt-in header X-Redwood-Tool-Compat: v1.
Author console UI for mapping preview and conflict resolution; add an admin audit log view.
notes: Trade-offs: We could force customers to adopt new tool_id model (easier long-term) but risk breaking unattended infra. Chosen approach: additive compatibility + opt-in header for strict mode.
Naming policy: store a canonical lowercased, whitespace/case-folded name for fast exact/alias matches. Keep original user-provided name for display.
Fuzzy-match algorithm: start with normalized Levenshtein threshold + token overlap; only used as last resort and must be explicitly enabled per-org.
Telemetry: add histogram for 'fallback_distance' and counter for 'fallback_used' with tags (customer_org, route, fallback_type).
Security: translations must not leak internal tool identifiers across orgs; tool_id namespaces required for multi-tenant isolation.
